message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"1","text":"Peter to James, the lord and bishop of the holy church: peace always from the Father of all, through Jesus Christ.\n\nKnowing, my brother, that you eagerly pursue what benefits all of us together, I urge and implore you not to share with anyone from the nations the books of my proclamations that I sent you, nor even with one of our own people before testing him. Rather, if someone, after being tested, is found worthy, then hand them over to him according to the method by which Moses also handed them over to the seventy who had inherited his seat. For this reason, the fruit of such safeguarding remains evident to this day. Those of their nation everywhere keep the same rule of monarchy and way of life, since in no way have they been able to be diverted into thinking otherwise by scriptures that point in many directions. For according to the rule handed down to them, they try to bring the inconsistent elements in the scriptures into alignment, if perhaps someone who does not know the traditions becomes numb before the utterances of the prophets that have many meanings. For this reason, they permit no one to teach unless he first learns how the scriptures must be used. Therefore, among them there is one God, one law, one hope.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τῷ κυριῳ καὶ ἐπισκόπῳ","chosen":"the lord and bishop","rationale":"The lowercase human honorific applied to James is distinguished from the divine title “Lord.”"},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ τοῦ τῶν ὅλων πατρὸς, διὰ Ιησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἐν εἰρήνῃ πάντοτε","chosen":"peace always from the Father of all, through Jesus Christ","rationale":"The Greek salutation is elliptical; the English preserves its source, mediation, and continuing peace without supplying a separate claim."},{"source_quote":"μήτε ὁμοφύλῳ πρὸ πείρας","chosen":"nor even with one of our own people before testing him","rationale":"ὁμόφυλος denotes someone of the same people or ethnic stock, while πείρα refers here to prior testing."},{"source_quote":"κατὰ τὴν ἀγωγὴν","chosen":"according to the method","rationale":"In this context ἀγωγή refers to the regulated procedure for transmitting the books rather than general conduct."},{"source_quote":"τῆς ἀσφαλείας","chosen":"such safeguarding","rationale":"The context concerns secure preservation and controlled transmission of teaching."},{"source_quote":"τῆς μοναρχίας καὶ πολιτείας","chosen":"of monarchy and way of life","rationale":"“Monarchy” preserves the source’s claim of single sovereignty, while πολιτεία can denote an ordered communal manner of life."},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ τῶν πολλὰ νευεσῶν γραφῶν","chosen":"by scriptures that point in many directions","rationale":"The rendering follows the contextually likely participle νευουσῶν, while retaining the image of writings pointing in multiple directions."},{"source_quote":"ναρκᾷ πρὸς τὰς τῶν προφητῶν πολυσήμες φωνάς","chosen":"becomes numb before the utterances of the prophets that have many meanings","rationale":"ναρκᾷ preserves the image of numbness or paralysis, and πολύσημος describes language capable of multiple meanings."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"νευεσῶν","issue":"The form is not readily intelligible here and appears to be a defective participle; the translation follows a contextual conjecture from νεύω.","proposed_reading":"νευουσῶν","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"πολυσήμες","issue":"The adjective does not agree morphologically with the accusative plural feminine noun φωνάς.","proposed_reading":"πολυσήμους","blocks_publication":true}]},{"reference":"2","text":"So that the same may also happen among us, give my books of proclamations to the seventy, our brothers, together with the corresponding mystery of the method, so that they may also equip those who wish to take up a share in the teaching. For if it does not happen in this way, our discourse of truth will be divided into many opinions. I know this not because I am a prophet, but because I already see the evil at its beginning. For some of those from the nations have rejected the lawful proclamation made through me and have embraced a certain lawless and babbling teaching of the enemy man. And while I am still alive, some have attempted, through various interpretations, to reshape my words so as to abolish the law, as though I myself thought this way but did not proclaim it openly. Far be it! For such a thing is opposition to the law of God, which was spoken through Moses and attested by our Lord with regard to its eternal permanence. For he said, “Heaven and earth will pass away; one iota or one stroke will certainly not pass away from the law.” He said this so that everything may come to pass. But they—I do not know how—claiming to represent my mind, attempt to interpret the words they heard from me more intelligently than I who spoke them, telling those whom they instruct that this is my view, something I did not even conceive. But if they dare to speak such falsehoods about me while I am still alive, how much more will those who come after me dare to do so once I am gone?","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τοῖς ἑβδομήκοντα, ἡμων ἀδελφοῖς","chosen":"to the seventy, our brothers","rationale":"The translation takes τοῖς ἑβδομήκοντα and ἀδελφοῖς as a single recipient phrase despite the supplied punctuation."},{"source_quote":"μετὰ τοῦ ὁμοίου τῆς ἀγωγῆς μυστηρίου","chosen":"together with the corresponding mystery of the method","rationale":"μυστήριον is retained as “mystery,” while ἀγωγή again denotes the controlled transmission procedure."},{"source_quote":"τὸ δἰ ἐμοῦ νόμιμον ... κήρυγμα","chosen":"the lawful proclamation made through me","rationale":"νόμιμος is rendered “lawful” because the following argument explicitly concerns preservation rather than abolition of the law."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ ἐχθροῦ ἀνθρώπου","chosen":"of the enemy man","rationale":"The rendering preserves both nouns and does not replace the phrase with an inferred personal or demonic name."},{"source_quote":"φλυαρώδη ... διδασκαλίαν","chosen":"babbling teaching","rationale":"φλυαρώδη characterizes the teaching as foolishly or emptily talkative."},{"source_quote":"ὅπερ ἀπείῃ","chosen":"Far be it!","rationale":"The optative expresses forceful repudiation of the preceding allegation."},{"source_quote":"περὶ τῆς ἀϊδίου αὐτοῦ διαμονῆς","chosen":"with regard to its eternal permanence","rationale":"The pronoun most naturally refers to the law, whose continuing validity is the immediate subject."},{"source_quote":"τὸν ἐμὸν νοῦν ἐπαγγελλόμενοι","chosen":"claiming to represent my mind","rationale":"The phrase describes a claim to know and speak for Peter’s own intention."},{"source_quote":"ἐμοῦ τοῦ εἰπόντος αὐτοὺς φρονιμώτερον","chosen":"more intelligently than I who spoke them","rationale":"The comparative adverb conveys the author’s sarcastic charge that others claim superior insight into his own words."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τοῖς ἑβδομήκοντα, ἡμων ἀδελφοῖς","issue":"The supplied comma separates words that most naturally form one dative recipient phrase, and ἡμων lacks the expected circumflex. The translation adopts that unified construction.","proposed_reading":"τοῖς ἑβδομήκοντα ἡμῶν ἀδελφοῖς","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"τὸ δἰ ἐμοῦ νόμιμον","issue":"The form δἰ places a breathing on the iota rather than the expected elision mark after διά.","proposed_reading":"τὸ δι᾽ ἐμοῦ νόμιμον","blocks_publication":true},{"source_quote":"ἐπχειροῦσιν","issue":"The verb appears to have lost the iota of the prefix ἐπι-.","proposed_reading":"ἐπιχειροῦσιν","blocks_publication":true}]},{"reference":"3","text":"So that nothing of this sort may happen, for this reason I urged and implored you not to share with anyone the books of my proclamations that I sent you—neither with one of our own people nor with a foreigner—before testing him. Rather, if someone, after being tested, is found worthy, then hand them over to him according to Moses’s method, by which he handed them over to the seventy who had inherited his seat, so that in this way they may keep their pledges and everywhere hand on the rule of truth, interpreting everything in accordance with our tradition, and so that they themselves, being dragged down through ignorance and drawn into error by conjectures arising in the soul, may not bring others into a similar pit of destruction. I have duly made known to you what seemed good to me; but as for what seems good to you, my lord, carry it out fittingly. Farewell.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"μήτε ὁμοφύλῳ μήτε ἀλλοφύλῳ","chosen":"neither with one of our own people nor with a foreigner","rationale":"The paired terms contrast someone of the same people with someone of another people."},{"source_quote":"κατὰ τὴν Μωϋσέως ἀγωγὴν","chosen":"according to Moses’s method","rationale":"ἀγωγή refers to Moses’s regulated procedure for entrusting the teaching."},{"source_quote":"τὰς πίστεις φυλάξωσιν","chosen":"they may keep their pledges","rationale":"The plural πίστεις can denote assurances or pledges of fidelity; “pledges” preserves the plural and suits the controlled transmission context."},{"source_quote":"τὸν τῆς ἀληθείας κανόνα","chosen":"the rule of truth","rationale":"κανών denotes the authoritative standard according to which the teaching is interpreted and transmitted."},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ τῶν κατὰ τὴν ψυχὴν στοχασμῶν","chosen":"by conjectures arising in the soul","rationale":"στοχασμοί are speculative inferences or conjectures, here located within the soul rather than in the received tradition."},{"source_quote":"εἰς τὸν ὅμοιον τῆς ἀπωλείας ἐνέγκωσιν βόθυνον","chosen":"bring others into a similar pit of destruction","rationale":"The translation preserves the source’s pit image and the qualifying adjective ὅμοιον, “similar.”"},{"source_quote":"ἔῤῥωσο","chosen":"Farewell","rationale":"The imperative literally wishes strength but functions conventionally as an epistolary closing."}],"source_issues":[]}]}
